name: hollerith-tabulator-census
description: Punched cards fed an electric tabulating machine that counted a national population far faster than hand tallying.

name: de-forest-triode-audion
friendly_name: De Forest Invents the Triode Tube
description: A three-element vacuum tube could amplify and switch signals, the building block of early electronic computers.

name: eccles-jordan-flip-flop
description: Two vacuum tubes wired to hold one of two stable states gave electronics its first memory cell.

name: bush-differential-analyzer
description: A room-sized analog machine at MIT solved differential equations with rotating shafts and gears.

name: zuse-z3-computer
description: The first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer ran on telephone relays in Berlin.

name: manchester-baby-runs-program
description: The first computer to run a program from electronic memory filled a room at a British university.

name: univac-i-delivered
description: The first commercial computer built in the United States went to the Census Bureau and later predicted an election.

name: kilby-first-integrated-circuit
description: Jack Kilby built a working circuit with several components on one slice of semiconductor, shrinking electronics for good.

name: ibm-system-360-announced
description: IBM bet the company on one family of compatible mainframes sharing software across a range of sizes and prices.

name: apple-ii-released
description: A colour-capable, ready-to-use microcomputer in a plastic case brought home computing to ordinary buyers.

name: ibm-pc-launched
description: IBM's open-architecture desktop machine with an Intel chip set the standard for personal computers.

name: arm1-processor-first-runs
description: A small British team's low-power RISC chip worked on its first try and later powered most mobile devices.

name: imac-launched
description: A translucent, all-in-one computer with no floppy drive revived Apple and made computers look friendly.

name: nvidia-geforce-256-gpu
description: Nvidia's GeForce 256 put transform and lighting on one graphics chip and popularised the term GPU.

name: ibm-quantum-factors-15
description: A seven-qubit molecule-based machine ran Shor's algorithm to factor a small number, a first for quantum hardware.

name: roadrunner-petaflop-supercomputer
description: Los Alamos's Cell-and-Opteron machine was the first supercomputer to sustain a quadrillion operations per second.

name: ibm-watson-jeopardy
description: IBM's question-answering supercomputer beat two champions on a televised quiz show.

name: raspberry-pi-released
description: A credit-card-sized, cheap single-board computer was launched to teach programming and sold in millions.

name: apple-m1-chip
description: Apple's own Arm-based system-on-a-chip replaced Intel processors in its Mac computers.

name: frontier-exascale-supercomputer
description: Oak Ridge's Frontier became the first supercomputer to top a quintillion calculations per second.

name: google-willow-quantum-chip
description: Google's 105-qubit chip showed error rates falling as qubits were added, a milestone for quantum error correction.
